title: Bridge replacement plan for southeast Centre Wellington
subtitle: Heritage designations, fees and charges changes, water conservation report, by-law enforcement, and County budget update.
overview: Council endorsed a preferred plan for four bridges in the southeast of the township. Three bridges (2-WG, 5-E and 7-E) will be replaced, and Bridge 3-E will be removed without replacement. Staff will publish a Notice of Project Completion for the study. Staff said replacement work is unlikely to begin for about three years, because the capital plan is already committed. The decision {{vote:m2}} affects farm travel, school buses, waste collection and local commute times.

Through the consent agenda, Council moved to designate three properties under the Ontario Heritage Act: 525 Union Street East, 249 Garafraxa Street East and 6475 Second Line. It also received the 2024 reports on water conservation, drinking water, quality management and by-law enforcement. Council approved amendments to the Fees and Charges By-law {{vote:m3}}.

The Mayor reported that the County of Wellington budget passed with a 3.7% increase, about $27 a year per $100,000 of assessed residential value. The County is also seeking funding for a climate change adaptation plan.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed Alternative No. 5, replacing Bridges 2-WG, 5-E and 7-E and removing Bridge 3-E without replacement, and directed staff to issue a Notice of Project Completion.
Council approved amendments to the Township's Fees and Charges By-law as set out in report COR2025-05.

Council confirmed its intention to designate 525 Union Street East, 249 Garafraxa Street East and 6475 Second Line under the Ontario Heritage Act, and received the 2024 water and by-law enforcement reports.
Council passed By-laws 2025-12 to 2025-15, designating the three properties and amending the fees and charges schedules.

debate: Council members asked how the closure of Bridge 3-E affects emergency response. Consultants said any added response time north of the bridge was about a minute, and that emergency drivers tend to use County roads. Staff said every property would still be reachable and that the Township keeps route maps for closures.

Community views on keeping Bridge 3-E closed were mixed. Some residents liked a quieter road, while others said the closure lengthens travel to businesses. Staff said farmers, including some from a neighbouring municipality, wanted all the bridges reopened because of detours onto County roads, and that their input helped set the replacement order.

One councillor was disappointed that the work could not be done all at once. Another asked whether the bridge replacement strategy should be re-evaluated. Staff said the 2025 asset management plan update will review bridge and culvert priorities, and that annual funding for them is still short.

On water conservation, councillors asked why the toilet rebate program had low uptake. Staff said the program launched over the holidays and that many applicants had newer toilets that did not qualify. Staff plan more promotion and may widen eligibility.

On by-law enforcement, a councillor asked about complaints. Staff said clean yards complaints rose sharply after the separate by-law was enacted, and that compliance is high through education and notice.
